full_text: Remember the barefoot Olympic champion? What he did next is harder to believe. Tokyo, 1964. Forty days before the Olympic marathon, Bikila has his appendix removed. He shows up anyway - and wins by more than four minutes. Another world record. The first person in history to win the Olympic marathon twice. Then, in 1969, his car overturned. He never walked again. So he found new sports: archery, table tennis - and in 1971, in Norway, he entered a sled race across the snow. He won that too. He died at 41, from injuries of that crash. Sixty-five thousand people came to his funeral. Today, Ethiopia's national stadium carries the name of the man who never stopped competing.
